title: Hydrogen-Bond-Engineered Analog Memory
question: Can hydrogen-bonded interfaces reduce trap-driven variation in analog synaptic updates?
teaser: Hydrogen bonding suppresses interfacial traps to stabilize analog conductance updates.
mechanism: PVA hydroxyl groups bond with surface iodides in CsPbI₃, reducing interfacial traps and stabilizing ion transport.
approach: Engineer the PVA–CsPbI₃ interface and compare analog conductance updates with device and array measurements.
evidence: DFT and electrical analysis; fabricated 7 × 7 crossbar; image-classification evaluation.
achievement: >8× lower interfacial trap density · ≈12.5 pJ/update · >10⁴ s retention at 85 °C.
myContribution: First author of the published study.
outcome: Hydrogen-bonded interface control produced linear and symmetric analog switching with device-to-array validation.
